newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end down, foreign interest seen lukewarm.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end down, foreign interest seen lukewarm.

text.p: South Korean shares closed lower on Monday afternoon on worries that foreigners would not jump into the market as actively as hoped for when the foreign shareholdings ceiling is lifted on Tuesday, brokers said.
The ceiling will be boosted to 20 percent for most stocks from the current 18 percent.
"Foreign investors are worried about South Korea's risk," said Jay Kwon, a broker with First Securities.
The composite index ended down 3.54 points to a provisional 789.67, after reaching a high of 804.68. Declining shares beat advancers by a nose, 435 to 430, while 116 were unchanged.

Analysts had predicted foreigners would inject between one and two trillion won into the bourse, but some market watchers now felt this was too optimistic. "I'm worried that the immediate inflow may not even reach 500 billion won," said a local fund manager who asked not to be named.
Brokers added that interest from foreign fund managers ahead of the ceiling boost was less than had been seen during previous ceiling expansion.
"Many are waiting till after the market in order not to tip off local investors, but still the number of phone calls from foreigners this time is much less," said a local broker.

Blue chips began the day upbeat, then lost steam as sentiment weakened. Yukong was an exception, ending at its upper limit of 21,000 won, up 1,100. The news it had designed an emmission filter for cars boosted interest in the shares.

Korea Mobile Telecom fell 18,000 won to 522,000 won. It does not have any shares available for further foreign investment. KEPCO fell 400 won to 27,300 on profit-taking. Brokers said investors were concerned that it had lose scarcity value since 18.5 million new shares will become available from Tuesday.
The December futures contract closed down 1.5 points to 83.30, while the KOSPI 200 index fell 0.46 point to 82.66.
